summary: Check a literal suffix at the end of a string.
documentation: endsWith compares a suffix case-sensitively. An optional endPosition treats that position as the string’s end for this comparison. It does not parse filenames, URLs, query strings or file contents.
inputs: A literal suffix and optional ending position.
returns: A Boolean indicating whether the suffix matches.
caution: A suffix check is not secure file-type detection. A .csv name can contain arbitrary content.
scenarios: Suggest an import workflow from a user-visible filename.
Recognize a documented suffix on an internal reference code.
Label archived exports before opening them.
title: Suggest the CSV import flow
problem: Input is a filename string. Return true only when it ends with the exact lowercase suffix .csv. Do not trim it or ignore case; .csv appearing in the middle does not qualify. This is a UI suggestion, not content validation.
goal: Use String.endsWith() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Compare the final characters with a literal .csv suffix.
